scenes.title: The plan

scenes.title: Key ideas
scenes.vo: First, Constant product (x times y equals k): works for any pair; spreads liquidity across all prices. Next, StableSwap: for assets that should trade near 1:1 (stablecoins, liquid staking token/ETH). Blends constant-sum (flat, low slippage near the peg) with constant-product (safety away from it), tuned by an amplification parameter. Then, Weighted pools: more than two tokens or uneven weights (for example 80 to 20), with invariant ∏ xᵢ^wᵢ equals k. An 80 to 20 pool has less impermanent loss on the 80% token. Also, Concentrated liquidity: positions in price ranges ("ticks"); the pool tracks the square root of price internally. On top of that, Hooks and dynamic fees: newer designs (for example Uniswap v4, 2025) let pools run custom code at swap time: dynamic fees, limit orders, oracles. Each hook is extra contract risk.
scenes.cap: First, Constant product (x·y=k): works for any pair; spreads liquidity across all prices. Next, StableSwap: for assets that should trade near 1:1 (stablecoins, LST/ETH). Blends constant-sum (flat, low slippage near the peg) with constant-product (safety away from it), tuned by an amplification parameter. Then, Weighted pools: more than two tokens or uneven weights (e.g. 80/20), with invariant ∏ xᵢ^wᵢ = k. An 80/20 pool has less impermanent loss on the 80% token. Also, Concentrated liquidity: positions in price ranges ("ticks"); the pool tracks √price internally. On top of that, Hooks and dynamic fees: newer designs (e.g. Uniswap v4, 2025) let pools run custom code at swap time: dynamic fees, limit orders, oracles. Each hook is extra contract risk.

scenes.title: Key ideas (cont.)
scenes.vo: And finally, L.V.R. (loss-versus-rebalancing): pool prices only update when arbitrageurs trade against L.P.s after prices move elsewhere. L.V.R. measures what L.P.s lose to that arbitrage, versus a portfolio that rebalances at market prices. For a full-range constant-product pool, L.V.R. about sigma squared/8 of pool value per year (sigma equals annual volatility). Fees must beat L.V.R., not just impermanent loss.
scenes.cap: And finally, LVR (loss-versus-rebalancing): pool prices only update when arbitrageurs trade against LPs after prices move elsewhere. LVR measures what LPs lose to that arbitrage, versus a portfolio that rebalances at market prices. For a full-range constant-product pool, LVR ≈ σ²/8 of pool value per year (σ = annual volatility). Fees must beat LVR, not just impermanent loss.

scenes.title: Worked example
steps: An ETH/USDC full-range pool with ETH volatility 80%/yr
With 12% fee APR, LPs keep ≈ +4%/yr before gas.
If volatility rises to 110%, LVR ≈ 15%/yr, and the same fees now lose money.
Higher-volatility pairs need much higher fee tiers.
scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. An ETH/U.S.D.C. full-range pool with ETH volatility 80% a year: the calculator gives L.V.R. about 8.0% a year. With 12% fee A.P.R., L.P.s keep about +4% a year before gas. If volatility rises to 110%, L.V.R. about 15% a year, and the same fees now lose money. Higher-volatility pairs need much higher fee tiers.
